subject: Archaeology
title: Underfloor Heating: The Hypocaust
description: One-minute skill: Underfloor Heating: The Hypocaust.

hook.text: Romans invented central heating 2,000 years ago. Hot air flowed under floors and through walls to warm entire buildings.

buildup.text: The hypocaust system raised floors on brick pillars. A furnace pushed hot air into the gap beneath the tiles.

discovery.text: Hollow clay tubes called tubuli lined the walls, carrying heat upward. Entire rooms were heated evenly.

twist.text: Slaves fed the furnaces day and night. The comfort of Roman baths depended on constant invisible labor.

climax.text: Modern underfloor heating works on exactly the same principle. Only the fuel source has changed.

punchline.text: We reinvented Roman heating and called it luxury. They called it a bathhouse.

quiz.question: How did the Roman hypocaust heating system work?
options: Steam from boiling water was piped through metal radiators
Hot air from a furnace flowed under raised floors and through wall tubes
Heated stones were placed in wall cavities to radiate warmth
